particulars.value: Recovery from Preferential, Undervalued, Fraudulent and Undervalued Transactions: In the event any transaction is avoided/ set aside by the NCLT in terms of Sections 43, 45, 47, 49, 50 or 66 of the IBC, and any amount is received by the Resolution Professional or the Corporate Debtor in furtherance thereof, such sums shall be for the benefit of the financial creditors and shall be a pass-through amount to the financial creditors. Such amounts received and/or receivable shall not form a part of the Successful Resolution Applicant Contribution under the Approved Resolution Plan or be reduced from the payment to be made by the Resolution Applicant to the financial creditors. The Resolution Plan shall further provide for the manner in which proceedings in respect of avoidance transactions, if any, under Chapter III or fraudulent or wrongful trading under Chapter VI of Part II of the Code, will be pursued after the approval of the Resolution Plan and the manner in which the proceeds , if any, from such proceedings shall be distributed as specified in Regulation 38(2)(d) of the CIRP Regulations. The cost of persuing these applications shall also be clarified. (b) Any infusion of fresh equity for - (a) improving operations, (b) debt repayment, (c) Capital expenditure & (d) any other purpose; shall be clearly specified along with the timelines for such infusion. (c) Any infusion of funds into the Corporate Debtor as part of the Resolution Plan shall be satisfactorily demonstrated including by way of firm financing proposals. (d) The Resolution Plan should also mandatorily specify source of funding as applicable including submission of a firm letter of commitment, or a signed sanction letter from any Bank / financial institution (as approved by RBI), as the case may be (“Letter of Commitment”), for the amount committed by the Resolution Applicant in the Resolution Plan as funds proposed to be utilized for making payments to Creditors as per the IBC.

particulars.value: Capability and Experience: The Resolution Plan should detail the experience of the Resolution Applicant and its capability to manage/ turnaround the Corporate Debtor. The Resolution Applicant should include: (a) Details of experience (nature of project, location, other operations details, equity shareholding, financial indicators for the preceding 5 (five) years etc.). Global experience may be included. (b) Prior experience in managing/ turning around of companies, including managerial competence, technical abilities and key management personnel experience along with supporting information and descriptions. Case studies may be appended to the Resolution Plan. (c) Management team to be appointed for the Corporate Debtor. Illustratively, appointment of turnaround experts; formation of Board and credentials of board members; appointment of Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer and Chief Financial Officer and other key personnel in sales and marketing finance, HR and operations, turnaround experts (with a write up on their profile); managerial competence and technical abilities; appointment of auditors (Statutory and Internal); retention of employees, etc.

However, in such an instance, the Resolution Plan may provide for issuance of new equity or quasi-equity. (b) It is clarified quasi-equity shall mean fund infusion by Resolution Applicant in the form of instruments, other than equity shares, which meet the following criteria: (i) they will rank sub-ordinate to the secured loans; (ii) the interest shall be cumulative, but will not paid before the financial creditors are repaid fully in accordance with the Resolution Plan;

particulars.value: Management of Corporate Debtor: (a) Resolution Plan shall mandatorily provide for a Monitoring Committee for supervising the implementation of the Resolution Plan post its approval from the Adjudicating Authority till the plan is fully implemented. (b) The Monitoring Committee shall compromise of 5 (FIVE) members i.e., Two representative of the Secured Financial Creditors, an Insolvency Professional (who shall be its chairman) and Two representative of the successful Resolution Applicant. (c) Except otherwise provided, all decisions of the Monitoring Committee shall be by way of a majority vote of all members. (d) The Resolution Applicant shall specify in the plan, the provisions for dissolution of monitoring committee; (e) In case a Resolution Plan(s) stipulates performance of any obligation by the Successful Resolution Applicant/ Corporate Debtor with respect to commercial commitments offered to Financial Creditors, pursuant to dissolution of the Monitoring Committee (for example, creation or perfection of security, redemption of debentures/ any other instruments and/or any other substantive/ procedural action proposed to be undertaken by the Corporate Debtor); the Resolution Plan(s) shall provide for appointment of nominee director of proposed by the CoC on the newly re-constituted board of the Corporate Debtor till such obligation is fulfilled by the Successful Resolution Applicant/ Corporate Debtor.
